description: Why the collector stopped collecting. Reads the collector_health measurement, which the collector writes to the local InfluxDB on every failed poll and once when an outage ends - so it is populated exactly when the AlphaESS API is unreachable and the container log is the only other record.

panels.description: Is collection happening right now? Green while the newest sample is under 5 minutes old, red past that -- the collector's poll loop never exits on failure, so "container up" says nothing. Matches the 'AlphaESS collector data stale' alert exactly. Ignores the time picker: this is always about now.
panels.title: Collector status

panels.description: Polls that raised an error in the selected range. A handful spread over days is normal upstream flakiness; a cluster is an outage.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "collector_health" and r.event == "failure" and r._field == "failures")
  |> group()
  |> count()
  |> yield(name: "failed_polls")

panels.title: Failed polls

panels.description: Distinct outages: one per run of consecutive failures that ended in a successful poll. An outage still in progress is not counted here yet - check 'Recent failures'.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "collector_health" and r.event == "recovered" and r._field == "failures")
  |> group()
  |> count()
  |> yield(name: "outages")

panels.title: Outages

panels.description: Longest gap in collection, first failed poll to the poll that recovered. Green under 5 minutes (one backoff cap), red over 30.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "collector_health" and r.event == "recovered" and r._field == "outage_seconds")
  |> group()
  |> max()
  |> yield(name: "longest_outage")

panels.title: Longest outage

panels.description: Time since the last failed poll. Large and rising is the healthy state.
panels.title: Since last failure

panels.description: Failed polls per interval, split by exception type. SSLError/TLS EOF points at the container MTU (local, fixable - see DEPLOY.md); ReadTimeout and HTTPError on a valid path point at the AlphaESS API itself (nothing to do but wait).

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "collector_health" and r.event == "failure" and r._field == "failures")
  |> group(columns: ["error_class"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: count, createEmpty: false)
  |> yield(name: "failures")

panels.title: Failures by error class

panels.description: The failures themselves, newest first, with the error the collector saw. This is the log line the Uptime Kuma alert is telling you about - readable from a phone, without opening a terminal.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "collector_health" and r.event == "failure")
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 100)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "error_class", "failures", "error"])
  |> yield(name: "recent_failures")

panels.title: Recent failures

panels.description: Completed outages, timestamped at the poll that recovered. 'Failures' is how many polls were lost; 'Duration' spans the first failure to that recovery.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "alphaess")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "collector_health" and r.event == "recovered")
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 100)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "failures", "outage_seconds"])
  |> yield(name: "outages")

panels.title: Outages

panels.description: Per-day sample coverage, recomputed here from raw power_readings rather than read from daily_cost/daily_energy -- those measurements silently drop any day under 96% coverage (the quality gate in pricing.py/efficiency.py) instead of writing a low number, so the days worth investigating are exactly the ones invisible there. Days are Netherlands calendar days (Europe/Amsterdam, DST-aware), matching day_window_utc() in pricing.py, so a red row here is the same day excluded from those dashboards. 'Gaps > 90s' counts inter-sample gaps over 3x the 30s poll interval; Coverage % charges only the excess above one interval for each such gap, plus any unsampled time before the first sample or after the last of the day -- identical accounting to pricing.compute_day()/efficiency.coverage_of(). Today's row, and any row the time picker cuts into mid-day, is judged against its elapsed portion of the day, not a fixed 24h. A day with literally zero samples (the collector fully down, not just flaky) has no row here at all -- check 'Failed polls' / 'Since last failure' above for that case.
